section.title: Introduction to Data Structures
section.content: A data structure is a way of organizing and storing data in memory to use them efficiently. The choice of a good data structure is crucial for the performance of an algorithm.

bulletPoints.point: ▶️ The choice depends on the problem to solve

section.title: Arrays
section.content: An array is a collection of elements of the same type stored in contiguous memory. Each element is accessible via its index. It is the simplest and most widely used data structure.

bulletPoints.point: ⚡ Direct access by index in O(1)

section.title: Records
section.content: A record is a structure that groups several fields of different types under the same name. It allows representing complex entities like a student with their name, first name and grade.

bulletPoints.point: ▶️ Each field has a name and a type
▶️ Example: Student { name: string, age: integer, grade: real }
▶️ Similar to struct in C or classes in Java

section.title: Pointers
section.content: A pointer is a variable that contains the memory address of another variable. Pointers allow creating dynamic data structures like linked lists and trees.

bulletPoints.point: ⚠️ Be careful with null pointers and memory leaks

section.title: Complexity and Choice of Structure
section.content: Each data structure has its strengths and weaknesses in terms of time and space complexity. You must choose the structure suited to the problem.

bulletPoints.point: ▶️ Time complexity: execution time of operations
🐢 Linked list: insertion O(1), access O(n)
🐢 Binary search tree: O(log n) on average

section.title: Linear vs Non-Linear Structures
section.content: Data structures are divided into two main categories: linear where elements are organized sequentially, and non-linear where elements have hierarchical or network relationships.

section.title: Static vs Dynamic Allocation
section.content: Memory can be allocated statically at compile time or dynamically at runtime. Each approach has its advantages depending on the program's needs.

bulletPoints.point: ▶️ Dynamic: variable size, flexible, via pointers
▶️ Dynamic allocation: malloc/new depending on language
⚠️ Mandatory release to avoid memory leaks
